summary: This is a Behat test class that automates browser testing using Chrome. It sets up a browser session in the constructor and provides a test step that clicks on a navigation menu item, taking screenshots before and after to verify the behavior.

explanations.11: FeatureContext extends MinkContext, which is a base class from Behat that provides methods for interacting with web pages in automated tests.
explanations.14: This declares a private property that holds the Mink browser automation object — think of it as the remote control for controlling the browser.
explanations.23: The constructor runs once for each test scenario and sets up a fresh browser session for that test.
explanations.25: Mink is being instantiated with a configuration array that tells it to use Chrome as the browser through a ChromeDriver connection.
explanations.27: A Session wraps the actual browser driver and provides a cleaner interface to interact with the browser.
explanations.28: ChromeDriver is the tool that actually controls Chrome; it connects to a Chrome instance running on port 9222.
explanations.41: The @Then annotation tells Behat that this is a test step that validates an expected outcome — 'Then' implies a verification step in the scenario.
explanations.43: This checks if a directory exists, and if not, creates it — a common pattern to ensure a folder is ready before writing files to it.
explanations.48: This takes a screenshot of the current page and saves it as a PNG file for visual verification of what the page looked like at that moment.
explanations.53: This uses a CSS selector to find all elements on the page that match the pattern (navigation links in this case), returning them as a collection.
explanations.59: This compares the text content of each link element to the menu name passed in; when it finds a match, it clicks that link.
explanations.65: This pauses execution for one second to give the website time to process the click and navigate to the new page before proceeding.
